title: Relative ampleness can be checked on an affine open cover of the base
statement: Let $h:Z\to S$ be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and let $N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose $S=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ is an affine open covering and $N|_{h^{-1}(U_i)}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] for every $i\in I$. Then $N|_{h^{-1}(V)}$ is ample for every affine open $V\subseteq S$.

source.place: Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), implication (3) implies (1). The conclusion unfolds f-ampleness into ampleness over every affine open of the base.

proof.text: Put $Z_i=h^{-1}(U_i)$, $h_i:Z_i\to U_i$, and $N_i=N|_{Z_i}$. The module $N_i$ is invertible by restricting local trivializations of $N$. Each $h_i$ is quasi-compact: an affine open $W\subseteq U_i$ is also an affine open of $S$, and $h_i^{-1}(W)=h^{-1}(W)$ is quasi-compact by the hypothesis on $h$. Apply [lem-trf-affine-base-ample-canonical-data] to each $(h_i,N_i)$, with affine target $U_i$ and the given ampleness. It gives separatedness and quasi-separatedness of $h_i$, the quasi-coherent canonical section algebra $\mathcal A_i$, its evaluation $\psi_i$, the equality $U(\psi_i)=Z_i$, and an open immersion $r_i:Z_i\to\operatorname{Proj}_{U_i}(\mathcal A_i)$.

source.place: Tags 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), affine-base part of (3) implies (5); 01VI (lemma-relatively-ample-separated); 0892 (lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample)(2), affine specialization.

proof.text: Each $h_i$ of Step 1 is the restriction $h^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ of $h$ over the open covering $S=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$, and Step 1 shows that it is separated. Separatedness of a morphism of schemes can be checked on such restrictions over an open covering of the target, with no quasi-compactness of the covering [lem-sfb-separated-lfp-target-open-locality]; hence $h$ is separated. A separated morphism is quasi-separated [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated], so $h$ is also quasi-separated. Together with the original quasi-compactness of $h$, these are precisely the prerequisites for the global canonical section algebra of Step 3 and for condition (2) of the canonical-Proj criterion.

source.place: Tag 01VI (lemma-relatively-ample-separated), proof: 'Being separated is local on the base'; Tag 01VJ (lemma-characterize-relatively-ample), proof of (3) implies (5): 'Hence f is separated'; schemes.tex Tag 01KP (lemma-characterize-separated) and the remark after Tag 01KK (definition-separated) that a separated morphism is quasi-separated.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-canonical-proj-open-cover-gluing] to the quasi-compact separated $h$, the invertible module $N$, the given affine covering, and the local canonical data of Step 1. It gives the ordinary quasi-coherent canonical section algebra $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}h_*N^{\otimes d}$ and evaluation $\psi$, with $U(\psi)=Z$ and canonical map $Z\to\operatorname{Proj}_S(\mathcal A)$ an open immersion. Together with Step 2's quasi-separatedness and the original quasi-compactness, these verify condition (2) of [lem-trf-scheme-ample-canonical-proj-criterion]. Its reverse implication gives $h$-ampleness of $N$, which means that $N|_{h^{-1}(V)}$ is ample for every affine open $V\subseteq S$, as required.
